text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- The U.S will urge strict respect of the Erdut agreement and protection of civil and national rights of the Serbs in Croatia, said U.S. Ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith.
- Yugoslavia signs three agricultural cooperation agreements with Macedonia during visit of Yugoslav agriculture minister Nedeljko Sipovac to Skopje.
- Skoda is ready to expand cooperation with Yugoslav firms, offering to invest in their privatisation. Total value of deals could reach $500 million.
- Serbian government to complete draft privatisation law by mid-May and submit it to parliament for adoption.
- Dinar continues to strengthen against the German mark on the black market exchange rate, one mark now fetches 3.5 dinars.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic receives religious community leaders in Yugoslavia for a traditional meeting.
- Annual meeting of presidents of Serbian courts to be held in Kragujevac.
NASA BORBA
- European Union to discuss granting autonomous trade measures to Yugoslavia at its ministerial council meeting next Tuesday.
- Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) expected to make changes in its leadership at today's main board meeting.
- Serbian oil industry Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS) to organise one-hour work stoppage demanding responsibility and replacement of management and measures to take company out of crisis.
- Members of the city ambulance independent trade union will organise protest gatherings at 1800 local time every day from April 26 over low and late wages.
- Some 400 workers of Popovac cement plant near Paracin organised protest demanding release of their fellow workers from prison. The eight were arrested when protesting against factory management.
- Pronounced shortage of ready cash has pushed black market dinar exchange rate up.
- Sartid metal works board of directors replaces managers after two fires in the plant in one month.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian government needs 15 billion dinars for regular pension payments this year, only 12 billion dinars covered.
- Council of Trade Unions of Yugoslavia President Dragan Radulovic says announced workers protest rally in Podgorica has nothing to do with politics.
- Serbian health workers trade union postpones work stoppage over late wages to May 12 from May 5.
- Trial of seven Bosnian Moslems on war charges continues in Zvornik court. Pathologists say bodies of killed Serbs had visible saw, axe and knife marks. Moslem-Croat Federation lawyers walk out.
- Depositors upset by bankers' proposals that interest should not be calculated on frozen hard currency savings even though there are no funds to pay out the principle.
BORBA
- Yugoslavia, Czech Republic sign memorandum on cooperation in transport.
- First trains from Sarajevo to Belgrade and Zagreb soon, says Bosnia railways director Smajo Salkic.
- According to draft law on concessions, natural resources will be offered to local and foreign investors for up to 30 years.
- Kostolac thermal power plant to spend nearly 70 million dinars for necessary overhaul before the forthcoming season.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Organised crime in Serbia on the rise. Drug, weapon and car smuggling most "profitable businesses" in the last six years in the Balkans.
- Serbian railways preparing for ownershp transformation. The state will decide to what volume public enterprises can privatise, but it will not be more than 49 percent.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- Vukasin Maras, the head of Montenegro's security service will not be replaced. The government considers he performs his duties professionally and within the law, said Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic in an interview to a Belgrade weekly.

- Road construction coordinating committee held its first session Wednesday chaired by Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic. It will prepare projects for construction of roads Belgrade-Podgorica-Bar (190km through Montenegro), Nis-Pec-Podgorica and and the 90 km Herceg Novi-Ulcinj coastal highway.
- U.S. finance ministry announced that the five Montenegrin ships blocked in American ports would be released on April 24.
- Montenegrin airlines will hold promotion flights - on April 24 to Belgrade, April 25 to Nis and May 7 to Bari, Italy.
- Montegrin trade unions to hold protest rally in Podgorica over social status of workers. -- Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
